_comment: Connector-specific edits to GENERATED/authored files that a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and banned anti-patterns absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

asserts.contains: report["credentials"] = "ERROR not verified: no credential is configured, so nothing was probed."
report["api"] = "not configured (base_url is a placeholder); set " + doctorBaseURLEnv + " to your own instance URL"

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For maxio the manifest gained: MAXIO_API_KEY, MAXIO_BASE_URL. server.json gained: MAXIO_API_KEY, MAXIO_BASE_URL. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: MAXIO_API_KEY, MAXIO_BASE_URL. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: The generator's hidden Cobra alias `create` is removed from the 16 commands listed in `why` whose POST deletes, cancels, disables, stops, rolls back or otherwise destroys or disrupts something, so `<parent> create` no longer runs them
handfixes.why: cli-printing-press gives a POST endpoint command the hidden alias `create`. On these commands the POST is destructive, so an agent that guessed the conventional verb (`<group> create`) ran the destructive call, and the alias appeared nowhere in help, agent-context or governance.md. Reproduced on origin/main 6416a241b against a local fake server: `maxio-cli subscriptions purge-json create sub_123 --ack 1` sent POST /subscriptions/sub_123/purge.json, `sentinelone-cli reports create` sent POST /reports/delete-reports and `tactical-rmm-cli agents shutdown create agent-42` sent POST /agents/agent-42/shutdown/. Fleet gate: tools/maintainer/check_command_tree.py, which walks the real cli.RootCmd() tree (137 such commands in 28 connectors on 6416a241b, 0 after). The canonical command names are unchanged; only the alias goes. A reprint re-adds it: remove it again. TestDestructiveCommandsDoNotAnswerToCreate fails while the alias is present. Commands here: invoices issue-json issue-invoice (POST /invoices/{uid}/issue.json); invoices refunds-json refund-invoice (POST /invoices/{uid}/refunds.json); invoices void-json void-invoice (POST /invoices/{uid}/void.json); proforma-invoices void-json void-proforma-invoice (POST /proforma_invoices/{proforma_invoice_uid}/void.json); subscription-groups cancel-json cancel-subscriptions-in-group (POST /subscription_groups/{uid}/cancel.json); subscription-groups delayed-cancel-json initiate-delayed-cancellation-for-group (POST /subscription_groups/{uid}/delayed_cancel.json); subscription-groups service-credit-deductions-json deduct-subscription-group-service-credit (POST /subscription_groups/{uid}/service_credit_deductions.json); subscriptions advance-invoice issue (POST /subscriptions/{subscription_id}/advance_invoice/issue.json); subscriptions cancel-dunning-json cancel-dunning (POST /subscriptions/{subscription_id}/cancel_dunning.json); subscriptions delayed-cancel-json initiate-delayed-cancellation (POST /subscriptions/{subscription_id}/delayed_cancel.json); subscriptions hold-json pause-subscription (POST /subscriptions/{subscription_id}/hold.json); subscriptions migrations-json migrate-subscription-product (POST /subscriptions/{subscription_id}/migrations.json); subscriptions prepayments refund (POST /subscriptions/{subscription_id}/prepayments/{prepayment_id}/refunds.json); subscriptions price-points bulk-reset-subscription-components (POST /subscriptions/{subscription_id}/price_points/reset.json); subscriptions purge-json purge-subscription (POST /subscriptions/{subscription_id}/purge.json); subscriptions service-credit-deductions-json deduct-service-credit (POST /subscriptions/{subscription_id}/service_credit_deductions.json).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: emit the `create` alias only for operations that create something.

handfixes.summary: export --output closes its output file on every return, including an API error: the open no longer shadows the named err of RunE.
handfixes.why: The generated `f, err := openExportOutput(...)` inside the --output block declared a new err, so the deferred close tested that inner (nil) err and never ran when the export returned an API error. With the output chokepoint the file is a filter pipe, and the unclosed pipe kept the process from exiting: `export clients --output f.jsonl` after a 401 hung (TestExportOutputReturnsAfterAnAPIError, seen failing 3 of 4 runs). Fleet note: every connector that took the ported chokepoint edit on export.go carries the same shadowing. Ported to maxio from the gradient 4.34.2 reprint (one credential layer across the fleet). handfixes.summary: The kit sees the resolved templated base URL (https://{site}.chargify.com with MAXIO_SITE filled in) as the one API origin, and a site that is not one DNS label shows noSiteOrigin, so no credential is sent anywhere.
handfixes.why: The ported guard pinned url.Parse(c.BaseURL); the unresolved {site} template does not parse, so the pin would be empty and every request refused. pinnedOrigin resolves the template first and refuses a site that could change the host (a dot, a slash, an @); a site changed after the client is built (sync --path-context, an MCP argument) cannot move the key. (maxio 4.34.2 reprint)

handfixes.summary: events record and bulk-record-events post to https://events.chargify.com/<MAXIO_SITE>/events/..., and that host is the one allowed origin besides the API base.
handfixes.why: The Events-Based Billing operations declare their own server https://events.chargify.com/{site}; the press bakes the variable's DEFAULT into the command path (https://events.chargify.com/subdomain/events/...; 4.24 shipped it too, and dropping the variable strips it), so every event went to the site 'subdomain', and the origin pin would refuse the events host outright. The generated paths keep {site} (tools/apply_edits.py events-site-resolved: events_record.go, events_bulk-json_bulk-record-events.go, internal/mcp/code_orch.go) and the client resolves it from MAXIO_SITE; pinsFor admits exactly the clean /<site>/events/ path prefix there (another site, dot segments, escaped paths, a custom MAXIO_BASE_URL: refused). (maxio 4.34.2 reprint)
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Teach the press to keep an operation-level server variable that shares a name with a global template variable as a runtime placeholder instead of baking its default into the command path.

handfixes.summary: Of every Maxio spec name, exactly Authorization, the card and bank fields (full_number, cvv, bank_account_number, bank_iban), the single-use payment tokens (chargify_token, payment_method_nonce), the vault references, the self-service page token and the webhook signatures read as credentials; billing data under names that look like credentials (an event key, a masked_card_number, last_four, uniqueness_token, stored_credential_transaction_id) never does. The rule is cliutil.SecretFieldName; the kit declarations are checked against it.
handfixes.why: The ported rule set carried domotz's names (SNMP communities as bare read/write, inventory key, activity-log user) and missed Maxio's: a card number, CVV, bank account number or IBAN an operator types into a payment-profile or signup request printed in --dry-run previews and the maxio_execute preview, while Event.key (payment_success) and the ACH authorizer's name were withheld. The names are pinned against the spec (testdata/maxio-spec-names.json, 832 names) in both directions, and any name the vendor DESCRIBES as a credential must read as one or be reviewed public. (maxio 4.34.2 reprint)

handfixes.summary: The documented Basic password x is never held: the client holds the API key half of the built header and not the password, header:authorization is an exempt identifier, and MAXIO_PASSWORD=x is not held while any other value is.
handfixes.why: The Basic payload <key>:x is held and its halves split, and MAXIO_PASSWORD reads as a credential name, so the constant x became a held value: every standalone x in output (and, through its encodings, every 78 and eA) printed the withheld marker. x is the same public constant for every Maxio account. Test seen failing first: seen/basic-constant-password-public-seen-failing.log in the run dir. (maxio 4.34.2 reprint)

handfixes.summary: The published MAXIO_USERNAME (the API key) and MAXIO_PASSWORD (x) pair keeps working on the 4.34.2 single-secret auth: MAXIO_USERNAME supplies the key when MAXIO_API_KEY is unset, MAXIO_PASSWORD other than x is refused without echoing it
handfixes.why: Press 4.34.2 renders Basic {token}:x from MAXIO_API_KEY only (spec x-auth-env-vars); the 0.1.x docs and manifest told operators to set MAXIO_USERNAME and MAXIO_PASSWORD, so an upgrade would have silently lost their credential. config.go is generated: tools/apply_edits.py re-applies the call and the envHasCredential line; the logic lives in internal/config/maxio_auth_compat.go. (maxio 4.34.2 reprint)

handfixes.summary: spec.json x-auth-env-vars [MAXIO_API_KEY] + x-auth-basic-password x: the client sends Authorization: Basic base64(MAXIO_API_KEY:x)
handfixes.why: Stock 4.34.2 reads the scheme description's constant password and renders one secret, but names it MAXIO_TOKEN (a name no doc, manifest or user ever used). Spec-encoded (tools/spec_fix.py): survives every reprint from this spec. (maxio 4.34.2 reprint)

handfixes.summary: CreateSubscription.prepaid_configuration and SubscriptionGroupSignup.bank_account_attributes take one JSON flag each (--subscription-prepaid-configuration, --subscription-group-bank-account-attributes), so every MCP input name fits the 64-character tool property grammar

handfixes.summary: One MRR snapshot (the site row and every per-subscription row) is fetched first and written in one transaction; a failed or unreadable /mrr.json, /stats.json or per-subscription page leaves no part of it, and mrr now drops a live answer whose stats read failed

handfixes.summary: Every SQLite handle goes through credkit.SQLDriver: internal/credsql registers the one driver and every sql.Open in store.go and platform/migration.go names it, the read-only opener included, which runs "select 1" because the kit's connection does not forward Ping. The MCP sql value cap moved from sqlite.Limit on a held connection to a DSN parameter (store.OpenReadOnlyValueCapped).
handfixes.why: A reprint regenerates store.go, migration.go and mcp/tools.go with sql.Open("sqlite") and sqlite.Limit, which would let a held credential reach the data db unchecked (class credential-persisted-outside-the-store).

asserts.contains: func OpenReadOnlyValueCapped(dbPath string, maxValueBytes int) (*Store, error) {

handfixes.summary: credkit.MCPHTTP writes every response the MCP HTTP server serves, refusals included. requireBearerAuthWithLimits runs a preflight that writes nothing (Origin, bearer, bounded body read), then credkit.MCPHTTP around a gate that answers the refusal it decided.
handfixes.why: A 401 or 413 written before the kit sees it is a frame the kit never checked (class replacement-protocol-frame-leaks-credentials, HTTP side); a reprint restores rejectMCPHTTPRequest, which writes outside the kit.

handfixes.summary: A --stdin request body is read before the command runs and its credential fields are held through credkit.HoldBody, then fed back to the command unchanged. A plain create's echo still prints and a pretty-printed body still works.
handfixes.why: Kit StdinFlags holds whole lines, which withholds a create's own response and refuses a pretty-printed body; exchange-online is the precedent.

handfixes.summary: A response's card, bank and token fields (the seven credentialFields, the vault references and the webhook signatures) are replaced right after the body is decoded in client.do, so no sink sees them and an ordinary subscription list is not withheld whole. The seven are held too; a vault reference or signature is not held, because a gateway's value can be as short as 1.
handfixes.why: Maxio returns vault_token on every subscription with a card: withholding the unit would make ordinary list commands unusable, and holding a value of 1 would withhold any output with that word.

handfixes.summary: A positional argument whose usage name is a credential (one-time-tokens <chargify_token>) is held before the command runs.
handfixes.why: The token is a path value, and an API error or a response can repeat the path.

handfixes.summary: The spec's example subdomain is no one's site: outside the verify and dogfood modes, an unset MAXIO_SITE stays unset, buildURL names the variable, and no request or key is sent.
handfixes.why: The generated default would send the operator's key to https://subdomain.chargify.com, a host they do not own.

handfixes.summary: Billed sums (revenue-mix and reconcile) leave out a consolidated parent invoice whose child segment is stored, through one bound list, revenue.SupersededParentsArg. A parent with no stored child still counts: it is the only record of the bill.
handfixes.why: InvoiceConsolidationLevel: a parent has no lines of its own and totals that aggregate its segments, so with sync --param consolidation_level=parent,child the amount was counted twice.

handfixes.summary: README.md, mcp-install.md and page.json say the ChatGPT desktop app runs this connector locally (STDIO) and that ChatGPT on the web, Microsoft 365 Copilot / Copilot Studio and the Gemini app are not supported by msp-skills yet, with a link to the hosted-gateway comparison; no paid-plan list, no Developer Mode recipe, no 'ChatGPT connects only to remote servers'.
handfixes.why: Docs fix approved 2026-11-03, following PR #502. OpenAI's MCP docs (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp) say the ChatGPT desktop app, Codex CLI and the IDE extension support MCP servers, add them as STDIO, and share MCP configuration; ChatGPT on the web uses remote MCP through plugins and does not read local Codex config. The old text listed ChatGPT plans, said ChatGPT connects only to remote servers, and on the reprinted connectors told users to host the connector over HTTPS for a Developer Mode connector and Copilot Studio; SECURITY.md pauses HTTP mode until each connector is reprinted. README.md, mcp-install.md and page.json are regenerated by msp-skills-publish onboard.py, whose template still writes the old ChatGPT text, so without this entry a re-onboard or reprint silently restores it.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Change the ChatGPT, Microsoft 365 Copilot and Gemini app text in onboard.py (cc-skills msp-skills-publish) so a regeneration writes this wording itself, then this entry can be retired.

asserts.contains: **Not supported by msp-skills yet.** ChatGPT on the web

### Does this work with ChatGPT?

Yes, in the **ChatGPT desktop app**.

asserts.not_contains: Microsoft 365 Copilot, Gemini, and any agent

handfixes.summary: Every CLI client is built with the on-disk response cache off, so a command re-run within five minutes reads the API's current answer.
handfixes.why: mrr sync and mrr now answered from the 5-minute cache: a changed site MRR was missed and the stale figure was saved under a fresh snapshot time (adversarial review, maxio 4.34.2 reprint).

handfixes.summary: An incremental sync's date-only bound is one day before the UTC date of the last sync, and endpoints whose date_field takes updated_at filter on it. A user's own date window (start_date, end_date and the datetime forms) replaces the stored bound, so every run asks what the first asked, and a user start bound under --since drops that date_field.
handfixes.why: Maxio reads start_date as midnight in the site's time zone and filters on a creation or issue date by default (spec.json /subscriptions.json, /invoices.json, /customers.json): evening changes at sites west of UTC, and every change to an older record, were never fetched.

handfixes.summary: The stored sync time moves only when the run covered everything since it: never after a run with a user param (a date window or any other filter) or a --since later than the stored time. Such a run also neither reads nor writes the resume cursor.
handfixes.why: The stored time asserts every change since it was seen, and the checkpoint is shared across filters. A narrowed run moved it, so the next plain sync started after it and an older record changed in between (a voided invoice) stayed stale until a --full run. A cursor left by a narrowed run also made the next plain sync skip that query's first pages and still read as complete.

asserts.contains: plainQuery, coversStored := syncRunReach(userParams, resource, sinceTS, sinceParam, lastSynced)

handfixes.summary: revenue-mix counts every usage kind spec.json LineItemKind documents (metered, prepaid usage and event-based components) as usage.
handfixes.why: prepaid_usage_component and event_based_component lines were counted as services.

handfixes.summary: a row the credential kit withholds from the store is skipped and named; the rest of the batch is stored, sync keeps walking, and the run still succeeds, naming the row ids on stderr and in its summary
handfixes.why: One withheld row aborted the whole batch transaction, and sync returned on it, so a single large ordinary record (or one that really carried a held credential) stopped the resource and every row after it was never synced (#612, hubspot-calls-crm). The row is still withheld; it is now named, and the watermark stays so the next run fetches it again. Re-applied after a reprint by replay_handfixes.py (recipe withheld-rows). synccpu (2026-11-09): a withheld row no longer fails the resource. mcp2 measured hubspot-calls-crm row 80663490159 turning the whole sync into exit 1, so the server never marked the connector synced. Now the resource ends stored with the ids named (stderr warning, a sync_warning rows_withheld event per page, and "withheld" in the summary), the run exits 0 when every other row stored, and the resource's checkpoint stays where the attempt began so the next run fetches the row again.

handfixes.summary: sync wraps the event writer its parallel workers share in syncSerialWriter (internal/cli/sync_event_writer.go), so two workers never call Write on it at once.
handfixes.why: The generated sync hands cmd.OutOrStdout() (or ErrOrStderr() in machine output) to every --concurrency worker, and each writes sync_start, progress and error events. os.Stdout tolerates that; the writers --deliver (a mirror into a bytes.Buffer) and --receipt-file / --audit-dir (a running SHA-256) install do not, nor does an in-process caller's buffer: Windows CI on PR #655 panicked in bytes.Buffer.grow from syncResource, and go test -race found 28 races on veeam. TestSyncWorkerPoolSerializesEventWrites pins it. A reprint regenerates sync.go and drops the wrap; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-event-writer-serialized).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#5369): the sync template should serialize the event writer its top-level worker pool shares, as its dependent path already does with lockedWriter.

handfixes.summary: the adaptive limiter's blind ramp raises only a rate the last Wait slept on, so sync's rate_rps reports a real pace
handfixes.why: On a header-less API the ramp multiplied the rate by 1.25 every 10 successes with no ceiling: mcp2's hubspot sync printed rate_rps 6.6e24 (about 2,500 requests), and after such a ramp a 429's halving could no longer slow a single request. A rate the requests never reach is no longer raised. Re-applied after a reprint by replay_handfixes.py (recipe limiter-paced).

handfixes.summary: a resource the vendor refuses this token (HTTP 403) is recorded as skipped and no longer holds store_status at partial; a resource that errored stays partial and is named.
handfixes.why: A 403 resource never completes, so its sync_state row stayed at 0 and store_status read partial for good after a clean exit 0 (#692). store_status now says complete_with_skips only when every other resource finished, and search, sql and sync_summary name what was skipped or failed. A reprint regenerates sync.go and mcp/tools.go and drops this; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-forbidden-not-partial).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: sync should record a resource the vendor refuses separately from one that failed (not filed yet).

handfixes.summary: sync_progress reports measured rows per second (rows_per_sec, and rate_rps as the same value); the limiter's ceiling is limiter_ceiling_rps.
handfixes.why: The generated sync printed the adaptive limiter's ceiling as rate_rps and as req/s on the human line, so 4.9 was reported while the sync stored 33 rows a second (#694). A reprint regenerates sync.go and brings it back; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-progress-measured-rate).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the sync template should report a measured rate and name the limiter's ceiling separately (not filed yet).

asserts.contains: func (t *syncThroughput) rowsPerSec(now time.Time, rows int64) float64 {

handfixes.summary: sync writes at most one sync_progress line per resource every 5 seconds (the first page always reports; sync_complete carries the final count), instead of one per page.
handfixes.why: Every write to stdout or stderr costs a full credential check whatever its size, and sync wrote one progress line per page: 74% of hubspot sync's CPU at a real server's pace (#696). A reprint regenerates sync.go with one line per page; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies the guard (fleet_handfixes.json sync-progress-throttled).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the sync template's per-page progress line should be throttled, as its dependent walk already is (not filed yet).

handfixes.summary: The <api>_search tool's description ends with the API's resource families (codeOrchSearchResources in internal/mcp/search_desc.go, from codeOrchEndpoints, capped at 300 characters).
handfixes.why: The generated description was the same in every connector and named no resource, so a host that ranks tools by words put other tools above <api>_search for "<api> <resource>" (#629; zammad_search ranked 13th of 45 for "zammad tickets"). A reprint regenerates code_orch.go without the call; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json mcp-search-desc-resources).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side (upstream PR named in fleet_handfixes.json): the code-orchestration template should build the <api>_search description from the endpoint registry's resource families.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Upstreamed as cli-printing-press #4647: every value-carrying branch of cliArgsFromMCP joins the value to its flag (--k=v, one element per list item), and the press generates TestCliArgsFromMCP_ValueCannotSmuggleBlockedFlag.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: The note paused HTTP mode until a reprint because the build served HTTP with no token. Press 4.34.0 HTTP mode refuses to start without <PREFIX>_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN, answers 401 without the right bearer, binds 127.0.0.1 by default and refuses a non-loopback address without TLS; onboard.py now writes HTTP guidance that follows the binary (cc-skills #14) and never writes this note, so the entry would fail on every re-onboard.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Press 4.34.0's cobratree mirror derives one blocked set per command (destination, input, mcp:write-flags, mcp:read-flags and root control-plane flags), leaves those flags out of the tool schema and refuses them, and any undeclared argument, by name.
